grade_reason: The main point is caught: the DeepSeek chip report, Huawei's half of a ~US$50 billion market, and OpenAI's Broadcom chip. But one Reuters rumour is split into three records (e1-e3), and e1 lacks the 'early stage' hedge, so the judge could weigh one source as three. e3 is labelled third_party_view with no originator when it is the same unnamed-source claim. Four original days are filled with the report day, including e6, which gives 2026-07-07 for an April launch and disclosure.
standard_doubt: Section 5.1 lists '华为现在占中国 AI 芯片市场约一半，这个市场约 500 亿美元' as new information to keep. In this article the sentence is a background aside ('Amid US restrictions ... Huawei has expanded its domestic market share and now controls around half of China's AI chip market'), and the US$50 billion size has been repeated for months. Taken as a fixed example, it makes a recurring background figure a keep every time an article repeats it. An analyst would keep it only when a new source or a changed figure appears.

Section 2 and D220 require an undated original day to be written as unknown, never the report day. For a wire rewrite published the same day ('According to Reuters, citing three sources ...'; 'Nvidia shares ... fell around 1.6% in US pre-market trading'), 'unknown' throws away the useful bound that the statement was made on or just before the report day. An 'on or before <report day>' form would keep that bound without claiming a date.
